manager_rule: Extend Rule 56's consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] counter to also increment for asymmetric single-member Kelvin failures. After each round R: if exactly ONE of /SENSEC{C}_HI or /SENSEC{C}_LO (but NOT both) appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines', AND cable C is NOT counted in kelvin_unrouted (the failing member has at least one track but still has ratlines — the asymmetric partial-routing case detected by Rule 50), increment consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] by 1, using the same counter and the same keepout injection threshold (count reaches 6, or the re-trigger threshold after a prior reset per Rule 56's protocol) as Rule 56 uses for symmetric failures. Apply Rule 57's escalated keepout geometry (per kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C]) when the threshold is reached. Log 'asymmetric_kelvin_stall_counter_increment' with: (a) round R, (b) cable index C, (c) the single failing member name, (d) consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[C] after increment, (e) whether a keepout was injected this round, (f) kelvin_keepout_escalation_count[C] at time of any injection. Rationale: Rule 56 triggers on symmetric failures (both members unrouted or both in failing_reasons) but not on asymmetric single-member failures that Rule 50 detects. Cable 2's /SENSEC2_HI has been persistently unconnected across at least rounds 110-111 while /SENSEC2_LO is routed, yet consecutive_kelvin_stall_rounds[2] has not advanced and no corridor keepout has been applied to cable 2. The same competitor-track displacement logic that justifies escalating keepouts for symmetrically-stalled cables applies equally to a persistently-failing single member — a foreign track is occupying the HI tap exit corridor whether or not the LO member was successfully routed around it. Without this extension, cable 2 can stall indefinitely in an asymmetric state and receive no spatial intervention until it degrades to a full symmetric failure.
